output:
The i.MX 95 Neutron NPU is a hardware accelerator designed to efficiently process machine learning workloads. Here are its key features and capabilities:

1. **Performance**: The NPU can achieve up to 2.0 TOP/s (Tera Operations Per Second) performance, with 1024 MACs (Multiply-Accumulate units) operating at up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC.

2. **Memory**: It includes a 1 MB local SRAM, which is available to the system outside of the NPU complex when not in use by the NPU.

3. **Activation Functions**: The NPU supports various activation functions, including ReLU, PreLU, LeakyReLU, and others, which are essential for neural network inference.

4. **Sampling and Reshaping**: The NPU can handle sampling and reshaping functions, which are useful for adjusting the dimensions of data tensors.

5. **Element-wise Operations**: It supports element-wise operations, which are fundamental for many machine learning algorithms.

For enablement details and constraints, see the documentation that is part of eIQ Toolkit at http://nxp.com/eiq. The NPU is an on-chip hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads. It works in conjunction with the chip's CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference. In addition to managing Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) compute blocks throughput, NPU also: • Optimizes arrangement of weights • Manages memory accesses • Provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions Enablement support for the eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU is provided with the eIQ Toolkit and eIQ Machine Learning (ML) Software Development Environment. Some of the features and operators listed in this chapter may not be enabled in eIQ software. See References for links to eIQ documentation that lists the features and operators enabled in the latest eIQ software. You can import your trained and quantized NN into eIQ Toolkit. The eIQ tooling generates an NPU-optimized model that can be integrated into an ML application running on the target device. 178.1.1 Block diagram Weight Decoder Rescaler/Shifter Activation Engine Data Canvas Bus Interfaces (built-in DMA) Buffers Control Compute Pipeline 0 Compute Pipeline n Figure 791. eIQ Neutron NPU architecture Table 1263. It can theoretically represent any function at any accuracy (up to full/bit-exact 16 bit), by increasing the number of table entries and/or the interpolation order. Note that an interpolator-based implementation of a function has a maximum throughput of at most 1 result every n+1 cycles, where n is the maximum order of the used polynomial fit. In contrast, the built-in activations functions provide up to 16 results per cycle and are therefore much faster. 178.2 Functional description 178.2.1 Mode of operation Neutron NPU contains local tightly-coupled memory (TCM) that enables it to retrieve data, weights, and control code. NXP Semiconductors Neutron NPU i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 11185 / 11263  178.2.1.1 Boot Neutron NPU is booted by any core downloading the firmware library into ITCM of NPU's built-in RISC-V core. After the firmware is downloaded, host core can make requests for NPU to execute an NN model. 178.2.1.2 Model execution Neutron NPU is fully autonomous from the chip-level system. It can access system memory and can fetch its own program code while it executes. It can also fetch required data and model parameters as needed. Neutron NPU reads model and input data from addresses specified by the CPU and writes results to the specified destination memory address. It can optionally generate an interrupt and/or a message when an operation completes. Neutron NPU has a mailbox through which any core can request job initiation and or query information. 178.2.2 Operator summary Table 1264.
